successCriteria.description: A signed-in session whose profile.role is MANAGER or ADMIN renders the wrapped children (no redirect).
A signed-in session whose profile.role is EMPLOYEE does NOT render the wrapped children and redirects away (e.g. to "/"), so an EMPLOYEE visiting the route directly sees no other employee's data.
A null session does NOT render the wrapped children and redirects to /login (delegating to the existing RequireAuth behavior).
The role is read from the auth session's profile via useAuth() — the implementation never decodes or inspects the JWT token.

A vitest suite beside the subject covers all four cases: MANAGER renders children, ADMIN renders children, EMPLOYEE does not render children (redirects), and null session redirects to login / does not render children.

constraints: The guard must read the role from the auth session's profile via useAuth() from web/src/modules/auth/index.ts; it must never decode or inspect the JWT token.
EmployeeRole must be imported from web/src/shared/types/index.ts (the existing shared types module) — do not redeclare the enum.
The guard must honor the isRestoring state from useAuth() (hold off on redirect while a stored token is being revalidated), mirroring the existing RequireAuth guard.
Files must live under web/src/presentation/guards/ (the presentation-guards module boundary), with the test beside the subject.
outOfScope: Route wiring of /approvals and the ApprovalsPage component (Phase 4), and the role-gated dashboard link (Phase 5) — this phase only delivers the guard and its tests.
Any backend/API role-scoping changes — the guard is a client-side presentation concern only.

ambiguities.description: Where an EMPLOYEE (or null-session) redirect should land: the phase allows either delegating to RequireAuth's /login redirect for null sessions, or redirecting to "/" for both. The EMPLOYEE case is specified as redirect away (e.g. "/"), but the exact target is left to the code agent.

entityInvariants.invariant: Renders its children only when the signed-in session exists AND profile.role is MANAGER or ADMIN; for any other state (null session, EMPLOYEE role) it renders a redirect and never the children.
The not-authenticated state is represented by a null session (no anonymous session object); role is carried on session.profile.role, never derived from the token.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Mirror the existing RequireAuth guard's structure and behavior (isRestoring hold-off, null-session redirect to /login, children rendering) — reuse its pattern rather than inventing a divergent one.
Consume the auth session via useAuth() and the AuthSession shape (session.profile.role) exactly as exported by the auth module.
Use the EmployeeRole enum values (EMPLOYEE/MANAGER/ADMIN) as declared in the shared types module.
Follow the established guard-test style (AuthProvider + MemoryRouter + Routes, fake IAuthService/tokenStorage/apiClient, waitFor assertions) used by the existing guard test.

integrationPoints.why: The guard obtains the signed-in session and its profile.role from the auth context; tests wrap the subject in AuthProvider.
The role comparison uses the canonical EmployeeRole enum values.
The null-session path delegates to / mirrors the existing authentication guard's redirect behavior.
